reason: 2.1.1 sets content: "\\" with [dir=rtl] nav[aria-label=breadcrumb] ul li:not(:last-child) ::after, a leftover from the old "/" divider. Because of the space before ::after, it matches the ::after of every element inside an rtl breadcrumb item except the last, not the item's own ::after, so each link or span showed a stray backslash in its own color after its text, next to the real divider, and a tooltip inside lost its caret. femto drops the rule. Rtl breadcrumbs use the same li::after divider as ltr, from --femto-nav-breadcrumb-divider, which the browser mirrors (">" draws as "<"). Ltr breadcrumbs are unchanged.
notes: Fixtures: every breadcrumb of components-nav.html in its rtl cells and its <div dir="rtl"> breadcrumb in its ltr cells, and the kitchen-sink.html breadcrumb in its rtl cells. where.dirs is not set because the dir=rtl island shows the change in ltr cells. femto accepts none or normal, however a browser reports the missing ::after. Probed with a standalone Selenium page in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160 beta, light and dark, at 390 and 1280: each gap of an rtl breadcrumb goes from the mirrored divider plus a backslash in the link color to a single centered divider, the same as ltr, a custom divider token stays honored, and a full computed-style diff changes nothing outside rtl breadcrumbs. Upstream issue picocss/pico#734.

reason: Consequence of rtl-breadcrumb-backslash: without the stray backslash, each link or span inside an rtl breadcrumb item except the last is narrower by the glyph's width, so the widths of those elements, their items and the list (and the origins that follow from them) match the ltr breadcrumb instead of 2.1.1's wider rtl one.
notes: Probed in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160 beta: rtl link widths go from 63.70/85.84/74.58 to 59.14/81.28/70.02 at 390 and from 78.14/104.34/91.08 to 72.61/98.81/85.55 at 1280, equal to ltr (4.56px and 5.53px narrower). Fixtures and where as for rtl-breadcrumb-backslash. Upstream issue picocss/pico#734.

reason: Consequence of rtl-breadcrumb-backslash: the item's own divider is absolutely positioned at the end of its narrower content, so its insets move and the divider sits centered in the gap, as in ltr, instead of beside 2.1.1's stray backslash.
notes: Probed in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160 beta: the divider moves from 2.5 to 3.5px off center to within 1px of center in every gap, at 390 and 1280, light and dark. Fixtures and where as for rtl-breadcrumb-backslash. Upstream issue picocss/pico#734.

reason: 2.1.1 gives [role=group] and [role=search] a bottom margin of --femto-spacing (1rem). In a nav item it zeroes margin-bottom for buttons, inputs, selects and dropdowns but not for groups, and the nav centers each item with its margin included, so a group or search form in a nav item sat about half a rem above the other items and made the nav a rem taller. femto zeroes the bottom margin of a group or search form that is the last element in its parent inside a nav item, so it centers with the other items and the nav keeps the height it has without a group. One followed by helper text (fieldset + small, whose small has a negative top margin) or by a second group keeps 2.1.1's 1rem, so the text is not pulled under the group. In an aside nav, or a dropdown menu in a nav, a group ending its item is now spaced from the next item like the other items, as an input there already was, and a nested ul[role=group] ending a nav item drops back to nav ul's own margin-bottom of 0. Groups outside a nav keep their 1rem margin.
notes: Fixtures: the "Groups" nav at the end of components-nav.html (a text item, a div[role=group], a form[role=search] and a button); the margin of the group and the search form goes from 16px at 390 and 20px at 1280 to 0px. The "Group helper" nav above it, a div[role=group] followed by <small> in one item, shows no difference, which checks that the :last-child guard keeps the margin. Probed with standalone Selenium pages in Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta at 1100 and 400px (roots of 19 and 16px), light and dark OS, ltr and rtl, data-theme light and dark, for a div[role=group], a form[role=search] and a fieldset[role=group] in a nav item: the group's center sat 9.25 to 9.5px and 8px above the text, link and button items, and the nav was 101.75 to 101.77px and 86px tall against 82.75 to 82.77px and 70px without a group; with the fix every offset is 0 and the nav is as tall as without a group. Focusing the group's input keeps its ring and moves nothing, and no x position or width changes. In an aside nav the gap below a group goes from 28.5 to 9.5px at 1100 (24 to 8px at 400), the item spacing; a group in a nav dropdown menu goes from 26.13 to 7.13px above the next item; a nested ul[role=group] ending a nav item loses its 1rem. A fieldset[role=group] or div[role=group] followed by <small> (in a nav, in an aside nav and with aria-invalid) and the first of two stacked groups compute as in the reference, and groups outside a nav, navs without a group and nav dropdowns are unchanged. Upstream issue picocss/pico#699.

reason: 2.1.1 gives every link in a nav item a negative margin on all four sides (nav li :where(a, [role=link])). Its next rule, for buttons, [role=button], [type=button], inputs and selects, resets margin-right, margin-bottom and margin-left but not margin-top, and a <button> already has margin 0, so only an <a role=button> kept the links' negative top margin. Its item came out shorter, it sat 3.5 to 4.25px above the links and the <button> or <input type=button> beside it, and a nav whose tallest item was such a link was 7 to 8.5px shorter than one with a <button>. femto adds nav li :where([role=button]) { margin-top: 0 } after that rule, so the link lines up with a button and a nav whose tallest item is such a link is as tall as one with a <button>. The :where() keeps the link rule's specificity, so an author's own margin-top on the link still applies. The rule is separate because the shared rule also matches label > input and label > select in a nav item, which keep their 0.25 * --femto-spacing top margin. aside li [role=button] { margin: inherit } and the breadcrumb and dropdown list link rules are more specific, so link buttons in an aside, a breadcrumb or a dropdown list are unchanged.
notes: Fixture: #cta, the <a role="button"> between a <button> and an <input type="button"> in the first nav of components-nav.html. Its margin-top and margin-block-start go from -8px at 390 and -10px at 1280 to 0px in Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta, in every leg, both directions and its hover state; at 1280 its top moves from 80.75px to 85px, level with the button and the button input. Probed with a standalone Selenium page in Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta at 375 (500 in Firefox), 1000 and 1400px, light and dark OS, ltr, rtl and data-theme light and dark: the link's top went from 3.5, 3.87 and 4.25px above an adjacent <button> to level with it, a nav of links and a link button grew from 63, 70.75 and 78.5px to 70, 78.5 and 87px (the height with a <button>), a link button in a [role=group] in a nav went from 9px taller than the group's button to the same height, and .secondary and .outline link buttons line up too. Buttons, button inputs, label > input and label > select, summaries in nav dropdowns, span and div[role=button], and link buttons in breadcrumbs, aside navs and dropdown lists compute as before. Upstream issues picocss/pico#496 and picocss/pico#568.

reason: 2.1.1 sets display: block on every ol, ul and li inside an aside, and half the nav element spacing as vertical padding and the full spacing as side padding on every li there. The rules exist to stack a nav vertically, but they match any list, so a list in an aside outside any nav lost its square or decimal markers (display: block drops list-item) and each one-line item grew from 1.5rem to 2.5rem with indented text. femto applies those rules only to lists with a nav ancestor (aside li:where(nav *) and so on, at the same specificity), so such a list renders like a list anywhere else: list-item, no padding and its markers. A vertical nav in an aside is unchanged, and so is an aside inside a nav. A bare aside > ul used as a sidebar menu without a nav wrapper gets markers, inline links and no item padding; wrapping it in a nav keeps the vertical nav style.
notes:
Fixture: the second aside of components-nav.html,

. Its li goes from display block to list-item and from 8px padding at 390 and 10px at 1280 on every side to 0px, in Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta, ltr and rtl, every leg and state. The aside nav above it, the kitchen-sink aside nav, the top navs, breadcrumbs and dropdowns show no new difference. Probed with a standalone Selenium page in Chrome Beta 158 and Firefox 160 beta at 500, 1000 and 1300px, light and dark OS, ltr and rtl, data-theme none, light and dark: a plain aside ul li and ol li go from block, 9px padding, 45px tall and no marker ink at 1000px to list-item, 0 padding and 27px with square and decimal markers drawn (on the right in rtl); a link there turns inline and a role=button loses its inherited 4.5px bottom margin. An aside nav (ul, ol, nested list, aria-current, role=button and a dropdown), a top nav, a breadcrumb, a top nav dropdown and nav > aside > ul are identical to the previous build in rect, display, padding, margin, colors, list-style, marker ink and hover and focus styles. The items of a dropdown inside a plain aside go from block to list-item with list-style none, the same rect and no marker. Upstream picocss/pico#646.
